entities.summary:
Antonio Caetani, seniore (1360–1412) was a Roman Catholic cardinal. As the son of Giovanni Caetani and his wife, Cecilia del Balzo, he followed in the footsteps of his father to enter the clergy.

Caetani rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming a cardinal in 1388. He played a significant role in the papacy of Pope Urban VI, supporting him against rival claimants.

One of Caetani's most notable achievements was his involvement in the Council of Constance, where he helped to bring an end to the Western Schism and restore unity to the Church. This event marked a turning point in the history of Christianity, as it brought about a period of relative stability and cooperation among Christian leaders.

Caetani's legacy extends beyond his role in the Council of Constance. He was also known for his charitable works, particularly in the area of education. During his lifetime, he supported the establishment of several schools and universities, which helped to spread knowledge and learning throughout Europe.

In 1412, Caetani died on January 20th, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and the world at large. His contributions to the Church's history and education continue to be felt today.
